hints: Each subset sum is between zero and the total weight; the total is at most 100,000.
Start with only sum zero reachable.
For each coin, update reachable sums downward so one coin cannot be counted twice.
analogy: Keep a checklist of sums possible so far; each coin adds its weight to every previously possible total.
example: Coins 2,3 can make sums 2,3,5, but not 1 or 4.
algorithm: Use a boolean array reachable[0..sum], initially reachable[0]=true. For each coin c, scan s downward from sum-c and mark reachable[s+c] when reachable[s]; list positive reachable sums.
correctness: Every subset is formed by deciding whether to include each coin; descending updates use only earlier coins, so every reachable sum corresponds to a valid subset.
complexity: O(nS) time and O(S) space, where S is total coin sum.
